questions.question: What makes a code review comment 'actionable'?
choices: It tells the developer specifically what to change and how
It references a code style guide
questions.explanation: An actionable review comment tells the developer exactly what to do: 'Extract this into a helper function' or 'Use a Map for O(1) lookups.' Vague comments like 'this is wrong' give no direction.

questions.question: Why is quality more important than quantity in code review comments?
choices: More comments slow down the CI pipeline
10 vague 'fix this' comments are worse than 3 specific, actionable ones
Managers only count comments for performance reviews
Automated tools can replace human comments
questions.explanation: Specific, actionable comments that identify real issues are far more valuable than many vague ones. Too many low-quality comments create noise and cause developers to ignore all feedback.

questions.question: A reviewer writes: 'This is terrible.' Is this a good review comment?
choices: Yes — it correctly identifies a problem
No — while technically feedback, it lacks specificity, actionability, and constructive framing
It depends on the reviewer's seniority
questions.explanation: Good review feedback must be specific (what's wrong), actionable (what to do instead), and constructive (framed as improvement, not criticism). 'This is terrible' fails on all three dimensions.
